prompts.L1:

A small antenna includes: a first element having a pair of conductors with a power feeding point; and a second element as a conductor arranged to sandwich a dielectric body. A part of the first and second elements has an inductance shape. A first resonance mode with a same current direction of the first element as the second element has a first resonant frequency. A second resonance mode with an opposite current direction of the first element to the second element has a second resonant frequency. A length from each power feeding point to the inductance shape is determined to hold the first resonant frequency within a range from a frequency slightly higher than the second resonant frequency to a high anti-resonant frequency of the second resonance mode, or a range from a frequency slightly lower than the second resonant frequency to a low anti-resonant frequency of the resonance mode.

A compact antenna comprises a first element formed from a pair of conductors that include power feed points, and a second element made of a conductor positioned so as to enclose a dielectric body between them. At least a portion of the first element and the second element is configured in an inductive shape.  

The antenna has a first resonance mode, in which current flows through the first element in the same direction as current in the second element, and this mode has a first resonant frequency. It also has a second resonance mode, in which current in the first element flows in the direction opposite to current in the second element, and this mode has a second resonant frequency.  

The distance from each power feed point to the inductive-shaped portion is set so that the first resonant frequency is maintained either within a range extending from a frequency slightly above the second resonant frequency to a high anti-resonant frequency of the second resonance mode, or within a range extending from a frequency slightly below the second resonant frequency to a low anti-resonant frequency of that resonance mode.
outputs.L3:
The small antenna includes a first element formed from a pair of conductors and provided with a power feeding point. This first element is configured to receive power from a feeding circuit and to function as one of the main radiating portions of the antenna.

The antenna further includes a second conductive element. The second conductive element is arranged in relation to the first element so that a dielectric body is sandwiched between them. In this configuration, the dielectric body is positioned between conductive portions of the antenna, thereby contributing to the electrical characteristics of the antenna, including its capacitance and resonant behavior.

At least part of each of the first element and the second element is formed into an inductance shape. This inductance shape may be, for example, a meandered, folded, coiled, or otherwise lengthened conductive pattern that increases inductance while allowing the antenna to remain compact. By providing such an inductance shape, the physical size of the antenna can be reduced while maintaining desired resonance characteristics.

The antenna is configured to generate at least two resonance modes. In a first resonance mode, currents flowing in the first element and the second element flow in the same direction. This in-phase current flow produces a first resonant frequency. In a second resonance mode, currents flowing in the first element and the second element flow in opposite directions. This opposite-direction current flow produces a second resonant frequency. Thus, the antenna can operate using different current distributions to obtain multiple resonant characteristics within a small structure.

The length from each power feeding point to the corresponding inductance-shaped portion is set so that the first resonant frequency is maintained within a specified range relative to the second resonant frequency and the anti-resonant frequencies associated with the second resonance mode. By appropriately selecting this length, the relationship between the first resonant frequency, the second resonant frequency, and the anti-resonant frequencies can be controlled. This makes it possible to stabilize the antenna’s operating characteristics, improve impedance matching, and achieve desired performance over a target frequency band while preserving a compact antenna size.
outputs.L4:
A compact antenna is configured to obtain stable resonance characteristics while reducing the overall size of the antenna structure. The antenna includes a dielectric body, a pair of feeding conductors arranged on or in relation to the dielectric body, and a second conductor positioned so that the dielectric body is disposed between the feeding conductors and the second conductor. The pair of feeding conductors are supplied with power at respective feeding points, and portions of the feeding conductors and/or the second conductor are shaped so as to define an inductance-forming portion. This inductance-forming portion may have, for example, a bent, looped, folded, meandered, or otherwise lengthened conductive path that produces a desired inductive component.

The antenna is designed to operate with two resonance modes. One resonance mode is mainly determined by the path extending from each feeding point toward the inductance-forming portion, while the other resonance mode is influenced by the conductive structure including the second conductor and the dielectric body. By appropriately selecting the distance or electrical length from each feeding point to the inductance-forming portion, the first resonant frequency can be controlled so that it remains within a desired range relative to the second resonant frequency. In particular, the first resonant frequency may be set close to the second resonant frequency, allowing the antenna to achieve a broader usable frequency band or improved impedance matching in a compact space.

Because the inductance-forming portion is incorporated into the antenna elements themselves, resonance adjustment can be performed without greatly increasing the external dimensions of the antenna. The dielectric body further contributes to miniaturization by shortening the effective wavelength within the antenna structure. As a result, the antenna can be made small while still maintaining favorable radiation efficiency, impedance characteristics, and frequency response. This configuration is especially useful for portable wireless devices, communication modules, and other equipment in which installation space is limited but stable antenna performance is required.
outputs.L5:
A small antenna is a compact device designed to transmit and receive radio frequency signals while taking up minimal space. Small antennas are commonly used in smartphones, wireless routers, GPS devices, Bluetooth equipment, smart home systems, drones, and many other modern technologies. Their compact size makes them ideal for portable and embedded applications where space is limited.

Despite their size, a small antenna can provide reliable performance when it is properly designed and matched to the operating frequency. Factors such as shape, material, placement, and surrounding components all influence how well the antenna works. Engineers often use designs such as chip antennas, loop antennas, patch antennas, and helical antennas to achieve good signal strength in a small form factor.

One of the main advantages of a small antenna is convenience. It allows devices to remain lightweight, sleek, and easy to carry. However, small antennas may have limitations, including reduced range, lower efficiency, and sensitivity to interference. To overcome these challenges, manufacturers optimize antenna placement and use advanced tuning techniques.

In today’s connected world, the small antenna plays an important role in wireless communication. From wearable devices to Internet of Things systems, it helps enable fast, efficient, and reliable connectivity in compact electronic products.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a small multiband antenna structure where a first element and second element create two resonance modes depending on current direction, and the feed-to-inductor length is set relative to the second resonant frequency and anti-resonance points.
counterfactuals.output:
A compact multiband antenna can be formed as a coupled two-element radiator fed at one end and loaded with an inductor.

The antenna includes:

- **A feed point** connected to an RF circuit.
- **A first radiating element** extending from the feed point.
- **A second radiating element** arranged close to, or connected with, the first element through an **inductive element**.
- A ground conductor or ground plane serving as the return path.

The first and second elements cooperate to produce two main resonance modes:

1. **First resonance mode — in-phase current mode**  
   Current flows on the first and second antenna elements in substantially the same direction.  
   This produces a lower-frequency resonance, because the effective electrical length of the combined structure becomes relatively long.

2. **Second resonance mode — opposite-phase current mode**  
   Current flows on the first and second elements in opposite directions.  
   This produces a higher-frequency resonance, because the current distribution creates a shorter effective resonant path and a different impedance condition.

The **inductor** is positioned along the structure so that the distance from the **feed point to the inductor** is selected with reference to the wavelength at the **second resonant frequency**. In practice, that feed-to-inductor length is set to be approximately an electrical quarter wavelength, or shorter than a quarter wavelength, at the second resonance frequency after accounting for dielectric loading and conductor geometry.

This length is also chosen in relation to the antenna’s **anti-resonance points**. The inductor and element lengths are adjusted so that anti-resonances, where the input impedance becomes very high and radiation efficiency may drop, do not fall inside the desired operating bands. Instead, the anti-resonance points are placed between usable bands or outside the communication bands.

In summary, the antenna uses two coupled radiating elements and an inductive loading point to create two resonant current distributions: one with currents flowing in the same direction and another with currents flowing in opposite directions. By properly setting the feed-to-inductor distance relative to the second resonance wavelength and shifting anti-resonance points away from target bands, the antenna can operate over multiple frequency bands while remaining physically small.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
